prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofing company for every Dallas homeowner — the right choice depends on your exact location, roof type, budget, insurance situation, and whether you want a local family business or a larger, manufacturer-certified contractor. I can help you find the best option for your situation. To start, I’ll give practical criteria, red flags, and next steps — and I can produce a short vetted shortlist if you tell me your ZIP code and a few preferences.

How to pick the best roofer
- Ask for license and insurance: they should show a Texas roofing license (or local county registration if applicable), general liability insurance, and workers’ comp or a waiver. Verify policy numbers with the insurer.
- Manufacturer certifications: look for GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred or similar — these matter for extended warranties.
- Written, itemized estimate: should list materials, brand/model, labor, permit fees, disposal, and timeline.
- Warranties: get manufacturer and workmanship warranty details in writing (length, transferability, and who handles future callbacks).
- Local references and recent photos: request 3+ local references and photos of completed jobs similar to yours.
- BBB and review sites: check BBB rating, Google/Angi/HomeAdvisor reviews, and recent online comments — focus on responsiveness and how complaints were resolved.
- Permits and inspections: reputable companies obtain permits and coordinate inspections; they should handle this.
- Payment terms: avoid contractors who demand full payment upfront. Typical structure: deposit, progress payment(s), final payment on completion.
- Written contract: include scope of work, start/finish dates, material specs, cleanup policy, payment schedule, warranty language, and a lien waiver on final payment.

Red flags
- No proof of insurance or license
- Only accepts cash or demands large upfront payment
- No written estimate or contract
- No physical business address or evasive about references
- Extremely low bid that’s far below others (often indicates low-quality materials or cutting corners)

What I can do for you
- If you give your Dallas ZIP code and basic preferences (asphalt vs. metal vs. tile, budget range, willing to use a certified installer, insurance claim or cash job), I can research and give a short list (3–5) of highly rated local roofers, summarize pros/cons, and include questions to ask each.
- Or I can provide a printable checklist and sample interview questions to use when contractors come to bid.

If you want a shortlist now, tell me:
1) ZIP code or neighborhood in Dallas
2) Roof type (asphalt shingle, metal, tile, etc.)
3) Any preference for certified installers (GAF/CertainTeed/Owens Corning)
4) Whether this is an insurance claim

Give me that and I’ll compile a tailored list of top-rated roofers and next steps.
